Create a NEW scientific-educational illustration for a beginner AWS infrastructure guide. The attached image is a STYLE reference only: keep its approachable isometric workshop drawing, fine navy outlines, cool off-white surfaces, cobalt details, subtle texture, and friendly human-scale objects. Make an actual explanatory chart with meaningful arrows and clearly separated labeled paths, not UI cards. Wide 3:2 landscape, opaque clean white background, generous 5% outer margin. Labels must be large, sparse, legible, exactly as requested. Do not draw or imitate AWS service logos: official SVG logos will appear in the page outside the image. No decorative charts, fake statistics, extraneous headings, or watermark.
Teach two ways to run code. Exactly two parallel horizontal lanes, never joined. Upper lane: a person at a laptop sends a request to a virtual server rack labeled "EC2", and that rack returns a completed work parcel. Lower lane: an event ticket arrives at a small workshop station labeled "Lambda", where a worker performs one task and hands over a result. Only additional labels: "Request", "Response", "Event", "Result". Make the contrast clear: operating a virtual server versus invoking managed event-driven code. The upper server and lower worker are literal friendly objects, not icons in boxes. Arrows follow the work from left to right.

Teach DNS separately from HTTP. Upper quarter: a browser laptop asks an address directory labeled "Route 53" a question and receives a destination answer; use two opposite arrows and the large label "DNS lookup". Separate this visually from the lower three quarters. Below, the same browser has TWO ALTERNATIVE outbound request paths: upper branch labeled "Assets" goes to an edge delivery station labeled "CloudFront", then to a file shelf labeled "S3" on a cache miss; lower branch labeled "API request" goes directly to a gate labeled "API Gateway", then to a workshop labeled "App". These branches must not join into a single serial chain. Route 53 is NOT in either HTTP path. Required labels exactly: "DNS lookup", "Route 53", "Browser", "Assets", "CloudFront", "S3", "API request", "API Gateway", "App". This simplified chart must prioritize correct branch directions and readable names.

Teach the distinction between permission and secret storage. On the left, a backend workshop computer labeled "Backend" makes a request toward a locked key cabinet on the right labeled "Secrets Manager". Above the middle of the request path is a staff badge and policy checklist labeled "IAM" with a thin downward arrow indicating it authorizes access. The key cabinet returns one key on a separate return arrow labeled "Credential" to the backend. Make it clear that IAM is the access rule and Secrets Manager is the locked storage. Teach pub/sub fan-out followed by queued work. At left an order workshop labeled "Order" sends one event ticket to a dispatch notice board labeled "SNS" in the center. From SNS two clear arrows branch to TWO SEPARATE job trays, each labeled "SQS". From the upper SQS tray an arrow leads to a worker at a laptop with an envelope, labeled "Email". From the lower SQS tray an arrow leads to a worker packing a parcel, labeled "Shipping". The arrows must be exactly Order to SNS; SNS to each SQS tray; each tray to its own worker. Never connect the two queues together, never imply that a queue does the work. Exact labels: "Order", "SNS", "SQS", "Email", "Shipping". The split is the main point; make all arrows clear and the two worker activities recognizable.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a NEW storyboard sprite sheet for a beginner AWS infrastructure guide. The reference image is a STYLE reference only. Match its friendly isometric shop/workshop, soft off-white materials, fine navy outlines, restrained cobalt details and paper texture. Important technical layout: one wide 3:2 canvas, a perfectly regular grid of equal-sized panels that fill the entire canvas edge to edge, no outside margin, no gutters, no panel borders. Each panel is a separate self-contained scene, with objects centered well inside that panel and a clean white background. Do not let any object or floor cross a panel boundary. No text, labels, letters, numbers, arrows, AWS logos, or watermark. The website will crop and display exactly one panel at a time, so every scene must read on its own. Consistent friendly shopkeeper and shopper across all panels.
Grid exactly TWO columns by TWO rows, FOUR panels, row-major reading order. Panel 1, top-left: a shopper at a laptop looks up a shop's destination using an address directory; the shopkeeper points to the correct address card. This represents a DNS lookup. Panel 2, top-right: the shopper requests a product-page photo from a small nearby delivery kiosk with blue-and-white awning and photo cards; this represents an edge content request. Panel 3, bottom-left: the delivery kiosk worker retrieves the original photo card from a separate organized file archive shelf; this represents a cache miss retrieving from S3. Panel 4, bottom-right: the shopper sees a product photo and a simple shop page on the laptop, satisfied that content has arrived. Keep the computer screen pictorial without readable text. All four are distinct, centered, complete scenes. Composition must obey the exact equal 2x2 panel grid.
